Simulation study of EBMF programs

This vignette evaluates empirical Bayes matrix factorisation (EBMF) programs against synthetic data with known ground truth. It is organised around input versions: the same simulation, EBMF, and program-validation pipeline is run on versions of the input that differ in how the planted modules are structured (background density and trait overlap, driver architecture, spurious hits, and structural zeros), so the recovery metrics are directly comparable across runs.

Each version is generated by simulate_trait(), which produces a trait object (the target trait plus driver and background traits) with known ground truth. The total number of SNPs is set via n_coloc_groups, and the total number of traits (rows) via n_traits. Planted modules occupy disjoint SNP sets in the clean version; overlap can then be introduced in trait space (trait_overlap, trait_effect_corr), in SNP space (driver_sharing), or within a module’s own SNP set (snp_driver_groups).

The generative parameters are calibrated to the messy marginals of a real pleiotropy matrix so the simulations are not trivially easy:

  • Background association magnitudes are drawn from a standardised heavy-tailed distribution and scaled relative to the planted module effects by background_effect_scale (a relative effect-size parameter, not a significance threshold), so e.g. background_effect_scale = 0.75 with effect_size = 6 gives background hits with typical magnitude ~4.5, some below and some above. Noise is encoded as absence (NA), not as a hard z-score floor.
  • Driver effects are heavy-tailed across traits (effect_tail), matching the across-trait heterogeneity seen in real modules.
  • Background trait densities are heavy-tailed per trait (background_sparsity_sd), so most background traits are observed at only a handful of SNPs while a tail is dense — reproducing the real per-trait sparsity distribution.
  • Driver traits can be split across SNP groups (snp_driver_groups) and can also act at the neighbouring module’s SNP set (driver_sharing), creating within-module and cross-module SNP structure.
  • Driver traits carry a low rate of background-scale spurious hits at off-module SNPs (p_spurious), and a fraction of each module’s true-support cells is removed entirely (p_structural_zero), i.e. real-data dropout inside a module.
  • The target-trait row is dense and significant at every SNP (target_pattern = "dense"), as real target rows are after orientation.

For every version, the identical battery is run: run_univariate_clustering() fits EBMF and keeps overlapping soft programs, and summarise_ebmf_programs() filters programs by lFSR, loading magnitude, size, similarity and trait-subsampling stability. The key output is a per-program table in which each validation check is its own column, so it is immediately visible which check failed for each program:

  • Programs with fewer than min_module_size filtered SNPs are dropped before any check.
  • confidence tier, checked in this order:
    • low when similarity_q >= similarity_q: the member SNPs are no more alike than random SNP groups of the same size, whatever the number of traits.
    • single_trait when the program passes the similarity test but its trait loadings rest on fewer than min_effective_traits effective traits. It is one trait’s hits, which noise produces too, so it needs a closer look.
    • high when similarity_q < high_similarity_q and connectedness >= high_connectedness; medium otherwise.
    A program counts as valid when its tier is high or medium.
  • excess_similarity / excess_connectedness (effect sizes against the random groups), factor_pve and replication (trait-subsampling Jaccard overlap) are reported alongside, not used for the tier.

Because the input now has realistic marginals, recovery is expected to be partial and noisy: the validation gates sit at the same levels that separate real modules from background, so only a subset of the discovered programs should be valid, and the pass rates below are the meaningful output for comparing input versions. The analysis settings below are fixed across versions; only the generative input changes.

Does this simulation exercise the gates in the regime real data uses them?

The validation gates act on the SNP similarity graph, so what matters is not whether the simulated matrix has realistic per-trait sparsity and magnitude marginals – it is whether the graph those marginals induce resembles a real one. Those are not the same thing, and matching the marginals is not sufficient.

simulated_graph_diagnostics() measures the simulated graph and real_bmi_graph_targets() carries the values measured on the BMI pleiotropy matrix. The row to read first is random_set_pass_rate: the fraction of random SNP sets whose mean internal similarity clears 0.3. On real BMI data that is about 0.94 – a random set of SNPs passes the old absolute gate almost always, which is why that gate carried no specificity. Where the simulated value is near 0, a random set can never pass, so a null simulation study cannot detect an uninformative gate and its false-discovery rate is close to un-failable by construction.

The two generative parameters that move this are background_corr (background traits sharing structure, so they contribute to SNP-SNP similarity at all – at 0 they are independent and random-signed and contribute nothing) and snp_pleiotropy_sd (per-SNP heterogeneity in how many traits a SNP is observed on, which is what brings the median pairwise overlap down towards the real ~3 and produces the sparse SNPs that carry high cosines).

Simulation design (ADEMP)

This study and its null companion follow the ADEMP structure of Morris, White and Crowther (2019, Statistics in Medicine 38:2074-2102, ). The elements are:

Aims. To evaluate the EBMF program-discovery pipeline when the truth is known: (i) how well planted modules are recovered (a model-selection target), and (ii) whether the validation gates stay quiet when no structure is planted (a testing target) — the latter is covered in investigation-univariate-null-simulations.html. Both aim to stretch the method by using realistic, messy marginals rather than a clean best case.

Data-generating mechanisms. Data are generated parametrically by simulate_trait(). It is calibrated so that background magnitudes, per-trait sparsity and driver heavy-tailedness match the marginal distributions of a real pleiotropy matrix (see the bullets below). Factors are varied as follows: p_active_background is crossed with trait_overlap (full grid) so background density is assessed at every overlap level; the driver-architecture, spurious-hit, and structural-zero axes are varied one at a time. The driver axis holds the clean baseline, while the spurious-hit and structural-zero axes are run against a harder baseline (trait_overlap = 0.5, p_active_background = 0.02) so contamination and dropout are not judged on trivially clean data. A full factorial over all axes was rejected because the resulting run count is computationally infeasible; the crossed background grid is the part where an interaction is a priori plausible. The number of SNPs (n_snps), traits (n_traits) and the noise level are fixed across versions.

Estimand / target. The estimand is the true SNP-to-module partition, ground_truth$module_of_snp (a selection target), with derived targets the number of modules K and each module’s SNP set. Recovery is scored by evaluate_univariate_simulation() (see R/evaluate_univariate_simulation.R).

Methods. A single pipeline is evaluated, with no comparators: run_univariate_clustering() fits EBMF and summarise_ebmf_programs() applies a confidence tier (size, similarity, connectedness), with factor strength and replication reported. Thresholds are fixed across versions and are the same as those used on real data.

Performance measures. With truth module_of_snp and predicted valid memberships, and writing truth/pred for the labelled partitions:

  • k_hat = |distinct predicted programs|, k_planted = |distinct planted modules|, k_error = |k_hat - k_planted|.
  • ari_structured: adjusted Rand index over module SNPs only (background excluded), with each SNP projected to its strongest assigned program. Computed by .adjusted_rand_index() in R/evaluate_univariate_simulation.R.
  • module_recall = mean_m max_p |module_m ∩ program_p| / |module_m| — the fraction of each planted module captured by its best predicted program; merge-fair, unlike ARI.
  • coverage = |{SNPs in any predicted program}| / n_snps.
  • background_absorbed = |{background SNPs in any predicted program}| / n_background — a SNP-level false-positive measure.
  • Tier rates: per-replicate fraction of programs passing size and similarity, and in each confidence tier (high, medium, low); valid is high plus medium.

Monte Carlo uncertainty. Each estimate is the mean over n_sim replicates (default 3; override with params = list(n_sim = ...) for fast test runs). The replicate is the Monte Carlo unit, and every estimate is reported with a Monte Carlo standard error and a 95% Monte Carlo interval. For a continuous measure the MC SE is sd / sqrt(n_sim); for a proportion it is sqrt(p(1-p)/n_sim); and n_sim can be chosen for a target MC SE via n_sim = p(1-p) / MCSE^2 (n_sim_for_mcse()). Common random numbers are used (one seed vector shared across all input versions), which lowers the MC SE of version-to-version differences. RNG states are recorded via the per-replicate seed in the estimates dataset.

Input versions

Each input version is produced by iterating over the generative parameter arrays in the params block: every array element becomes one version, paired arrays are iterated in lock-step, and the first element of each array is the baseline. p_active_background is the exception — it is crossed with trait_overlap, so every background density is evaluated at every trait-overlap level. The versions fall into four groups, each stressing one aspect of the planted structure; the driver-architecture axis holds the others at their clean baseline, while the spurious-hit and structural-zero axes are run on a harder baseline (trait_overlap = 0.5, p_active_background = 0.02):

  • Background density × trait overlap (p_active_background × trait_overlap / trait_effect_corr): the full grid of background association density against the fraction of each module’s driver traits shared with the other modules (correlated, trait_effect_corr, but non-identical effects).
  • Driver architecture (snp_driver_groups / driver_sharing): splitting each module’s SNP set into groups (each driver trait acts on one group) and letting some driver traits also act at the neighbouring module’s SNP set.
  • Spurious hits (p_spurious): background-scale off-module hits in the driver rows.
  • Structural zeros (p_structural_zero): a fraction of each module’s true-support cells removed entirely (NA), emulating real-data dropout inside a module.

Null simulations (K = 0, no modules planted) are covered separately in investigation-univariate-null-simulations.html.

Aggregate results

Across all replicates and programs of each version, the tables below report the recovery metrics and, for every validation check, the fraction of programs that passed it. Estimates are averages over 3 replicates and carry a Monte Carlo standard error in parentheses (ADEMP; Morris, White & Crowther 2019): the replicate is the Monte Carlo unit, so every number here is an estimate and the MC SE quantifies its uncertainty. valid is the fraction of programs that passed all checks.

high, medium, single trait and low are the shares of programs in each confidence tier; valid is high plus medium.

Program-level validation checks

For each version, every program found across the replicates is listed by replicate and then by confidence tier (green high, orange medium, grey single trait, red low).

Each program is also scored against the planted module it overlaps most (on its gated SNPs): % module found is the fraction of that module’s SNPs the program recovered, % module missed its complement, and % not module is the fraction of the program’s SNPs that are not in that module (background or other-module SNPs pulled in). % module found + % module missed always sum to 100%. Under high trait_overlap a program that correctly merges two modules matches only one, so its % not module rises even though it is recovering real structure — read these alongside the merge-fair module_recall in the Aggregate table.

similarity lift is the member SNPs’ mean similarity over that of random SNP sets of the same size, and factor PVE % the share of the matrix variance the program explains; the similarity test compares the first against its size-matched null.

Notes for interpreting runs

  • Fast test runs. A production render is long: n_sim = 200 over the 23 input versions is thousands of EBMF fits, and the cost of a single fit is dominated by summarise_ebmf_programs (permutation calibration + stability), not by the repetition count alone. quick (default TRUE) trades reporting rigour for speed, not breadth: it always runs the full 23-version grid, but caps n_sim at 3, sets n_null = 1, and disables stability — about 1 min, and enough to see which input parameters move the recovery metrics before committing to a full-depth run. To iterate quickly, override params:
    • params = list(quick = TRUE) (default) — full 23-version grid, cheap internals (n_sim = 3, n_null = 1, no stability); about 1 min.
    • params = list(quick = FALSE, n_sim = 20) — full 23-version grid at higher fidelity (real n_null/stability) but reduced repetitions.
    • params = list(quick = FALSE) — the full study (n_sim = 200, full n_null/stability); long, intended for a production render. Lowering n_null and n_stability_rep gives the largest speed-up.
  • Each input version comes from iterating the generative parameter arrays in the params block; arrays are iterated in lock-step with their paired parameter, and the first element of each array is the baseline.
  • p_active_background is crossed with trait_overlap (full grid), so the background-density effect is evaluated at every trait-overlap level; the driver-architecture axis holds the others at their clean baseline, while the spurious-hit and structural-zero axes run on a harder baseline (trait_overlap = 0.5, p_active_background = 0.02).
  • module_recall and coverage preserve overlapping valid EBMF memberships.
  • Planted modules occupy disjoint SNP sets; module overlap in these simulations comes from shared trait drivers (trait_overlap, with correlated trait_effect_corr), or from driver traits acting at the neighbouring module’s SNP set (driver_sharing).
  • snp_driver_groups splits each module’s SNP set into groups, each driver trait acting on only one group; with more groups a module’s drivers are only recoverable from their own SNP subgroup, fragmenting the module’s signal.
  • p_spurious adds background-scale off-module hits to the driver rows, so driver traits carry contamination outside their own module.
  • p_structural_zero removes a fraction of each module’s true-support cells entirely (NA), so a module’s signal is only recoverable from the cells that are present — real-data dropout inside a module.
  • The generative marginals are calibrated to a real pleiotropy matrix: driver effects are heavy-tailed across traits (effect_tail), background densities are heavy-tailed per trait (background_sparsity_sd), and background magnitudes are scaled relative to the modules by background_effect_scale. With this difficulty level, recovery is expected to be partial and noisy — that is what makes the per-check pass rates informative.
  • ari_all and ari_structured use each SNP’s strongest assigned program as a hard projection, so they remain conventional partition metrics.
  • factor_pve and replication are reported only; the tier uses size, similarity_q and connectedness.
  • lFSR and magnitude thresholds determine assigned SNPs before similarity, factor-strength, and posterior-evidence calculations.
  • Every aggregate number is a Monte Carlo estimate over n_sim replicates and is reported with its Monte Carlo SE (ADEMP). Reduce n_sim only for test runs; the MC SE in the tables will show the resulting loss of precision.
  • Replicates use common random numbers: the per-replicate seed (sim_seeds) is shared across input versions and recorded in tier_summary$sim_seed, so the study is reproducible and version-to-version differences are more precise than independent seeds would give.
  • Null simulations (K = 0, no modules planted) and the false-discovery rates of the validation checks under pure randomness are covered in investigation-univariate-null-simulations.html.
